items: Removal Authority: Members of SHRC are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed by the President of India.
Jurisdiction Exclusion: SHRC cannot investigate any case currently being inquired into by the NHRC or any other statutory commission.
Time Bar: The Commission cannot inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act was committed.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Both NHRC and SHRC were constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
The NHRC has jurisdiction over the entire country, whereas SHRC covers subjects under the State List and Concurrent List.
The Chairperson and members of NHRC are appointed by the President, while those of SHRC are appointed by the Governor.
Although appointed by the Governor, SHRC members can be removed ONLY by the President of India.
Both commissions hold the powers of a civil court, but their recommendations are advisory in nature and not binding.
